summary: Concepción Airport (CEP) is a small regional airfield serving the town of Concepción in the Santa Cruz Department of eastern Bolivia. Located in the lowland tropical plains of the Chiquitania region, it primarily handles short-haul domestic flights and general aviation. The airport supports connectivity to remote communities in this sparsely populated but ecologically significant area near the Chiquitos dry forests.
faqs:
Q: What type of airport is Concepción Airport?
A: It is a small regional airport primarily serving domestic flights and general aviation within Bolivia.

Q: Which airlines operate at Concepción Airport?
A: The airport is mainly used by regional Bolivian carriers offering domestic connections, particularly to Santa Cruz.

Q: Is Concepción Airport suitable for international flights?
A: No, it is a small domestic facility without customs or immigration services for international travel.

Q: What is the geographic setting of the airport?
A: The airport sits in the tropical lowlands of eastern Bolivia, in the Chiquitania region known for its unique dry forests and Jesuit mission heritage.
transport_tips: Ground transportation at Concepción Airport is limited, so arranging a taxi or pickup in advance with a local contact is recommended. The airport is located a short distance from the town center of Concepción, and most travelers rely on informal transport or hotel-arranged transfers. Roads in the region are unpaved in many areas, so travel times can be longer than expected, especially during the rainy season.
local_tip: Visit during the dry season (May to October) when dirt roads are most passable, and take time to explore the nearby Jesuit mission towns like San Ignacio de Velasco, which are part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site just a few hours away.
